messages.author: 5b321281ac94aa14
messages.subject: error "system is computationally singular"
parts:
Hi,

when I run the common Factor multivariate GWAS model with SNP effects for PGC data for OCD, MDD, ADHD, and ASD I get one of the following errors:

When running in parallel: (pfactor<-commonfactorGWASpar(SNPcov, estimation = "DWLS"))

Error in { : task 4 failed - "system is computationally singular: reciprocal condition number = 1.06082e-17"
Calls: commonfactorGWASpar -> %dopar% -> <Anonymous>

when running serially: (pfactor<-commonfactorGWAS(SNPcov, estimation = "DWLS"))
Error in solve.default(t(S2.delt) %*% S2.W %*% S2.delt) :
  system is computationally singular: reciprocal condition number = 1.28174e-17
Calls: commonfactorGWAS -> solve -> solve -> solve.default

This seems to point towards a problem of linear dependent columns (strongly correlated variables), which means that the matrix is not invertible?
Any idea how to solve that issue?

Thanks, Nora

messages.author: d6d83e22ef3ba9f1
messages.subject: Re: error "system is computationally singular"
parts:
Hi Nora, 

I've added an update to the commonfactorGWASpar function that now lets you specify the tolerance for the different inversions that occur throughout the function. If you re-install the function you can now set the tolerance to a much liberal threshold (e.g., 1e-30) as below:

pfactor<-commonfactorGWASpar(SNPcov, estimation = "DWLS",toler=1e-30)

Let us know if you run into any other issues!

-Andrew
